title: Sigil and Thorn
premise: Kestrel Underhill, exiled twelve years ago for a storm-calling that killed her mentor, sells harmless charms in the magic-free city of Vellharrow. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin working again, Kestrel discovers she is the living sigil that unsealed them — her exile was engineered by the Thorn Court, who need her blood to wake their war-god before winter seals the world in eternal silence. Torn between Maerin, the duty-bound warden hunting her, and the truth that her own guilt-fueled prayers started everything, Kestrel must choose: destroy the gods' gate and lose her magic forever, or claim it and become the tyrant everyone fears she already is. She shatters the gate at the cost of her power, ending the divine war before it begins, and chooses exile no longer — staying in Vellharrow, powerless but free, with Maerin at her side.
about_author: Lena Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in northern coastal towns before turning to fiction. Sigil and Thorn is her second novel, following the acclaimed The Saltwright's Daughter.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Winter
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In frost-bound Vellharrow, Kestrel sells luck-knots and fever-charms, hiding her storm-born scars beneath gloves. A child's prayer at her stall is answered — impossibly — by a whisper of wind. Emotional beat: quiet dread; the past she buried has begun breathing again.

chapters.title: Prayers with Teeth
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. More answered prayers ripple through the city; a drowned fisherman walks home. Kestrel investigates the old shrine where it began and finds her own sigil burned into the altar stone. Emotional beat: horror and recognition — this is her mark, her doing.

chapters.title: The Warden's Warrant
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. Warden Maerin Vale, tasked with purging magic from Vellharrow, traces the miracles to a charm seller he has quietly admired for years. Ordered to arrest her, he hesitates. Emotional beat: duty grinding against reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, flashback-woven. Arrested, Kestrel recounts the storm that killed her mentor Aldous and earned her exile from the Stormhold. Maerin listens, unconvinced her crime was as simple as reported. Emotional beat: confession as both shield and wound.

chapters.title: What the Cell Remembers
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. In her cell, Kestrel sleep-talks in the old tongue, and frost blooms through stone. Maerin finds records sealed by the Thorn Court — her trial was tampered with. Emotional beat: a warden discovering his institution is the true criminal.

chapters.title: The Broken Cage
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Agents of the Thorn Court attack the gaol to take Kestrel alive; Maerin breaks her out rather than surrender her. They flee into the salt marshes. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the first fragile trust between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: Road of Ashes
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Journeying toward the ruined Stormhold for answers, the pair bicker, share fire-warmth, and evade thorn-masked riders. Kestrel's magic flickers dangerously near Maerin. Emotional beat: intimacy kindling inside mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Hollow Tower
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the abandoned Stormhold, they find Aldous alive — aged, half-mad, kept by the Thorn Court as bait. He reveals Kestrel is not merely a storm-caller but a living sigil, born once a century. Emotional beat: grief curdling into fury at being used all along.

chapters.title: Blood in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. Aldous explains the Thorn Court engineered Kestrel's exile to season her guilt, because a sigil's power opens only through despair. Maerin realizes his own superiors are Court agents. Emotional beat: betrayal of everything he served.

chapters.title: Thornmarch
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Court's riders corner them; Aldous dies holding the pass so they can escape, asking forgiveness Kestrel cannot yet give. Her grief cracks open a sliver of true storm-power. Emotional beat: mourning fused with terrifying awakening.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. Sheltering in a glacier shrine, they learn the truth of the ancient war: the gods were imprisoned by mortal sacrifice, and the long winter is their prison failing. Kestrel's opened sigil accelerates the thaw of the seal. Emotional beat: awe dwarfed by responsibility.

chapters.title: An Honest Lie
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. To protect Maerin, Kestrel slips away at night to surrender herself to the Court, believing she can deceive them from within. Maerin wakes to cold ashes. Emotional beat: love expressed as self-sacrifice, and its cruelty.

chapters.title: Court of Thorns
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Brought before Lady Vessia of the Thorn Court, Kestrel plays the broken penitent while learning the ritual: her blood on the gate at midwinter will crown Vessia as the war-god's vessel. Emotional beat: icy performance masking rising panic.

chapters.title: The Man Who Followed Storms
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. Maerin defies his order, burns his warrant, and tracks Kestrel across the white country, gathering unlikely allies — smugglers, hedge-priests, an exiled god-tongue singer. Emotional beat: a dutiful man choosing treason with open eyes.

chapters.title: Chains of Guilt
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Vessia strips Kestrel's defenses, forcing her to relive Aldous's death until despair nearly completes the sigil. Kestrel clings to one memory — Maerin's hand in hers — and holds the gate shut. Emotional beat: the darkest hour survived by love.

chapters.title: Midwinter Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Maerin's ragtag allies assault the Thornmarch citadel during the solstice rite; Kestrel turns the ceremony against itself, storm-light tearing the hall. Emotional beat: chaos, courage, and the two of them finding each other amid fire.

chapters.title: Vessia Ascendant
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. Vessia drinks the half-spent ritual and becomes something vast and wrong; Maerin falls defending Kestrel, gravely wounded. Kestrel faces the choice laid bare: close the gate forever or seize the god's power. Emotional beat: sacrifice made visible in blood and snow.

chapters.title: The Unmaking Word
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Inside the gate's vision, Kestrel meets the imprisoned gods and understands they are as much prisoners as tyrants. She speaks the unmaking word, dissolving the divine realm — and her own magic with it. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; power renounced, identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The winter breaks; Vessia, mortal and hollow, is taken by her own Court. Powerless Kestrel tends the wounded, anonymous among survivors, unsure she deserves the peace. Emotional beat: exhaustion, humility, the strange lightness of emptiness.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. Recovering, Maerin refuses promotion and instead petitions to repeal Vellharrow's magic ban, using evidence of the Court's crimes. Kestrel watches him fight the system that shaped him. Emotional beat: hope rebuilt brick by stubborn brick.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Offered restoration of her name and a place in the new order, Kestrel instead reopens her charm stall — honest trinkets now, no magic needed. Maerin visits, off-duty, awkward and warm. Emotional beat: ordinary joy chosen over glory.

chapters.title: Sigil and Thorn
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, epilogue. On the first spring market day, rain falls clean over Vellharrow. Kestrel ties a luck-knot for a child whose prayer goes unanswered — because it doesn't need answering. She and Maerin walk home together. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; love without duty's shadow, identity without power's price.
